data.name: 868-HACK
data.detailed_description:
868-BACK crowdfunding!

868-HACK is 868-BACK! I'm developing a sequel, back it on backerkit today (they won't let me put a link here but just search 868-BACK and you'll find it).


PLAN.B

PLAN.B expansion available!


Acerca do jogo

You are a computer hacker. You steal precious data while the world sleeps. Siphons are your lockpicks. Progs are your guns.
Connect to the sectors.
Download the data.
Escape, or be deleted alive.

reviews.review:
If you're like me, you probably came here when you saw 868-BACK. Back to what? Or from what? From [strike]corporate life[/strike] hiatus, and to H4XXING. Of course. Or... to the past, since this game came out in the halcyon days of 2015, when we had no idea what's coming to us.

So: is it worth playing more than a decade later? Yes, but mainly as an entrée to playing 868-BACK. It is a small, develishly difficult game that's surprisingly clever and deep; and once you manage to wrangle it, you'll find yourself wishing for something like this, but bigger. And more of it.

And that's exactly what 868-BACK is. This, but bigger and more. But it's fundamentally the same thing, so let's decompile it and take look at the code.

A gauntlet of 8 levels made out of 6x6 grids reminiscent of classic roguelikes (we're talking ADOM classic, not Binding of Isaac classic): turn-based, stuff moves when you do, things get to your face to attack you and so on. You can attack like a rook in chess - as long as there is a line of sight, you can use the turn to pew the baddie. There are four kinds of baddies, and all of them have some kind of twist to them: one moves twice in a row, one can move through walls, one is invisible unless you are in the same row or column, and one takes 3 hits instead of 2.

And they just keep coming.

Your first few runs will probably end almost instantly, and you'll find yourself saying "What? All of a sudden I'm dead???". That's because you can take a whole lot of... 3 hits, and attack only one thing at a time. Which, when you break it down, means that:
- being surrounded by 3 enemies is instant death
- fighting two guys at once will reduce you to near-death if you're lucky, kill you if not
- even fighting in a chokepoint isn't safe since some enemies move twice, while others will just go through walls to  get to you.

And, of course, to get anything at all, you have to siphon data cubes which spawn multiple enemies at -once-. As many as 9 enemies. Plus, every new sector auto-spawns enemies on entry, and very quickly you'll find yourself facing a large group. Impossible, right?

What gives you a very minor fighting chance is the usage of progs. Think of them as special abilities or spells. You start with just one, and they cost energy and creds to use. And they don't seem all that strong, either. Push enemies away? Kill all guys that overlap with something else? Make this particular type of enemy explode? How am I supposed to-

Oooh, you can push enemies on top of each other and [i]then[/i] use that overlapping kill ability? I see what's going on here.

Every completed run unlocks a new prog, which in turn creates new strats. You can - if you want - unlock all progs for free, just for the hell of it, you can even re-lock them, why not. It doesn't necessarily make anything easier, since which progs you'll find is random in the end. And there is no meta progression. You just need to git [strike]commit[/strike] gud.

Of course, all of this applies to 868-BACK too, but in that game you do multiple of these gauntlets [strike]back to back[/strike] one after another, with modifiers that both make everything more difficult and give you more situational (but permanent) tools to play with. So it really isn't any easier.

It's frustrating, but it frankly slaps. A good way to see if you're going to like 868-BACK. And, to make things more delicious, if you play these games back to- IN ORDER, 868-BACK becomes a bit of an ode to... aging, of all things. But that's a line of thought for another day.
